topic: A neighbor asks to use part of the yard for a garden
text: The boundary I've known, the space I've claimed, is shifting. They come, these others, their hands reaching out, ready to reshape the earth I tread. The ground, once mine alone to wander, to know as deeply as the hollows beneath my paws, now carries the scent of tomorrow's change. It presses in, this alteration, a challenge to the very air I breathe. I circle the edges, my steps tight and quick, a guardian of what was, what must remain. The world narrows, and yet, the line must hold. My presence, a silent protest, a stance against the encroaching new.
